name: Martini
tagline: The film set for AI videos: people and agents generate, review and cut together, over MCP, CLI or API.
description: Martini's hosted MCP puts an agent on the same canvas and multi-track timeline the director, editor and producer have open — over MCP, the `martini` CLI or the HTTP API — so the people a shot is for can see, judge and change it. Video and image models from several vendors run on that canvas; every asset records how it was made (model, prompt, references, takes, edits, and the person or agent behind it), and spend is tracked per person, agent, project and model, with caps per member and per project. A Library of characters, props and locations carries continuity across shots and projects, and the cut exports as an MP4 or as XML for Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve or Final Cut Pro. Martini Bar exposes the same surface to a studio's own tools (script breakdowns, character bibles, prop libraries built in Claude Code or Lovable) and bills generations to the studio's own fal key. The public tool manifest lists 104 tools.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http --scope user martini https://www.martini.film/mcp

auth.key_url: https://www.martini.film — sign in with your Martini account (browser OAuth for MCP; `martini login` device code for the CLI; Settings → API keys for the Generation API)

caveats: Free allows only public projects, and a personal project starts with link sharing on (anyone with the link can edit); visibility "private" needs Pro or Team.
Generation spends olives or your fal credits and cannot be undone; generate_nodes, enhance_draft and upscale_assets quote first, so keep approvals on.
MCP needs a browser OAuth step, so shell agents should use the CLI's device-code login; the /mcp-core profile still returns HTML, so use /mcp.
Not for one throwaway clip nobody will review, live video, or cutting camera footage with no generated shots.
notes: Remote MCP server maintained first-party by Martini (YC W26). Plans at launch prices on 26 Oct 2026 (martini.film/bar): Free at $0 includes MCP, CLI and API with your own fal key but only public projects, so do not put a client's unreleased work on it; Pro ($25 a month) adds private projects and Studio ($125) a team workspace with permissions, both after a 30-day trial that needs a card. On fal-key plans generations bill to your fal account at fal's prices, and olives, Martini's credits, cover models not on fal plus set shots, voice creation, chat and agent work; olive-only plans also exist. Martini's own guidance says it is the wrong tool for one throwaway clip nobody will review, live video, or cutting camera footage with no generated shots. Re-checked 26 Oct 2026: https://www.martini.film/mcp answers POST initialize with 401 and a Bearer challenge whose protected-resource metadata names a Supabase authorization server, and the Claude Code command above is still the one the vendor's setup page prints. The tool count is now checkable from outside: GET https://api.martini.film/v1/tools answers without a key with the 104 tools every account can invoke (41 marked read-only, 95 also in the core profile); tools/list after sign-in remains the authority for your account. That manifest's create_project description also states the sharing default: a personal project starts with link sharing on, so anyone with its link can edit, unless the agent passes visibility "private", which needs a Pro or Team plan; a team project is always private. Several tool names from earlier releases are gone — model lookup is get_models (list, resolve a natural-language name, or inspect) and reusable subjects now live in the Library (get_library, edit_library) — so prompts or scripts written against list_models, resolve_model or create_subject will fail. The CLI (npm @martini-film/cli 0.5.0, MIT, Node 20.10+) signs in with a browser device code and saves a 90-day per-device key; it caches the server's tool list, so a tool added server-side becomes a command without an upgrade, and `martini init --write` installs a Martini skill under .claude/skills and .agents/skills. Martini's own guidance tells shell-equipped agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI) to prefer the CLI even with the connector installed, and the connector repeats that in-session. The Generation API (@martini-film/client 0.11.0, martini-client 0.4.0 on PyPI) reaches a narrower model list than the tools — Seedance 2.0 and 2.5, Wan 3.0, Grok Imagine 1.5, MiniMax H3, Nano Banana 2 and a few more — and per the vendor's llms.txt comes with every fal-key plan, Free included, but is on request for olive plans; MCP and CLI work on every plan. generate_nodes, enhance_draft and upscale_assets start nothing until called again with a server-computed quote's planHash; other generation tools such as create_node_and_generate rely on your MCP client's write-tool approval, so leave approval on. The core profile at https://www.martini.film/mcp-core, for which the Claude Code page now prints its own install command, still does not answer as an MCP endpoint on 26 Oct 2026: POST initialize returns the marketing page as 200 text/html, and the protected-resource metadata declares only /mcp. Use the full endpoint. The public github.com/martini-film/mcp repo holds client setup docs only (last pushed May 2026); server source is private. Setup docs cover Claude Desktop/Web, Claude Code, Codex, ChatGPT, Gemini CLI, Cursor, Hermes, OpenClaw, and generic Streamable HTTP clients.

name: Nomi
tagline: Open-source desktop workbench your agent directs: storyboard, generate, cut on a timeline.
description: Nomi is a local-first Electron workbench that exposes its own production surface over MCP, so Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Pi, or WorkBuddy can create a project, lay out shots on a canvas, draft and price a generation, clear a paid confirmation gate, and land the result on an editable timeline. The model layer is bring-your-own: hosted providers come pre-wired, and anything OpenAI-compatible or a local ComfyUI graph slots in beside them. That combination is rare — most studio-tier servers in this directory are hosted products that own the models, whereas here the agent directs software on your own machine against whatever engines you are already paying for. Durable production runs make it more than fire-and-forget: the agent can start a run, review and revise scripts and storyboards, and decide creative gates, while budget, export, and publishing stay with the human in the app.

install.stdio_command: Multi-step: install the Nomi desktop app (Nomi-mac-arm64.dmg, Nomi-mac-x64.dmg, or Nomi-windows-setup.exe from GitHub Releases), launch it once so it mints the local token, then use Model Integration > Connect AI Programming Assistant to register the bundled stdio server with your client. Do not hand-write the config: Nomi signs a per-machine, per-client proof into it. No published `claude mcp add` one-liner.

auth.key_url: No key for the MCP link — a local token is written to ~/.nomi/capability-core/token on first launch. Model providers still need their own API keys, entered in the app.

caveats: Desktop only (macOS and Windows x64, no Linux); the app registers the server itself, and signed configs cannot be copied between machines.
By design the agent cannot approve budgets, paid submits, rough-cut acceptance, export or publishing; those decisions come back to the app.
AGPL-3.0 with a commercial licence on request, one personal GitHub account, and a Chinese-only MCP guide.
The tool surface was rebuilt in Sep 2026, so older configs and prompts will not match, and every generation bills the provider key you configured.
notes: The tool surface was rebuilt in September, so older configs and saved prompts will not match it. The docs now count 24 tools, collapsed from 42 one-verb tools on 2 Sep 2026. Every read goes through `nomi_read`, canvas writes go through `nomi_canvas_edit` under a project lease, and a single generation is plan → preview → gate → execute. The `nomi_generate`, `nomi_add_nodes` and `nomi_get_run` names this entry used to list are gone. `nomi_canvas_plan` was retired on 5 Sep and `nomi_layout_read`/`nomi_layout_write` on 14 Sep. You can no longer copy the config between machines or clients: Nomi writes signed `NOMI_MCP_CLIENT` / `NOMI_MCP_CLIENT_PROOF` values bound to one machine and one client. A bare `NOMI_MCP_STDIO=1` entry can still list tools, but Nomi treats it as `external` and it cannot start real production runs. The old scripts/nomi-mcp.mjs path now exits with a migration message. By design the agent cannot approve budgets, per-shot paid submits, rough-cut acceptance, export or publishing. Those decisions come back to the app. Very active: ~520 stars, v0.22.1 released 26 Sep 2026, pushed 27 Sep 2026. It is still a single personal GitHub account, not an org. Licence: AGPL-3.0 for current releases, with a separate commercial licence on request, so shipping a derivative product means negotiating a licence first. Desktop-only: macOS arm64/x64 plus Windows x64, no Linux build. Releases now include electron-updater manifests. This pass did not recheck whether the builds are code-signed; earlier ones were not. The MCP guide is Chinese-only. 'Local-first' covers projects, assets and keys, but the guide itself notes that prompts and inputs still go to whichever provider you configured, and every generation bills that provider's key.

name: FilmLab
tagline: Hosted film lab: storyboard, generate, review, and export, with the price shown before each run.
description: FilmLab is the generative workbench attached to TheFilmRadar, a German-language industry platform for DACH film and TV crews, and it exposes its whole ten-stage pipeline over one OAuth-gated remote MCP. Thirty-seven tools cover project and pipeline context, auto-storyboarding, image and clip generation in batches, a review queue with contact sheets and continuity checks, a full location board that can generate variants and panoramas from a reference image, and sequence assembly through to export profiles and render jobs. The two things that distinguish it from the rest of the studio tier are the review stage — assets get a verdict before they reach a sequence — and cost preflight, which quotes credits before a run rather than after. Reading, browsing, and project creation cost nothing, so an agent can survey a project before anything is spent.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http filmlab https://mcp-lab.thefilmradar.com/mcp

auth.key_url: OAuth against a FilmRadar account at https://lab.thefilmradar.com — no API key and no token to paste

caveats: Closed source, one operator, German-first docs and MCP page, and no registry release since Aug 2026.
It does not name the models behind lab_generate and lab_animate, so you buy credits without knowing which engine renders them.
lab_delete_location is destructive, so scope the agent's permissions; credits expire after three months.
There is no anonymous access, so the tool names come from the docs, not a live tools/list.
notes: New and unproven: published to the official MCP registry on 2026-08-17 as com.thefilmradar/filmlab, with three versions shipped that same day and 1.1.1 still current as of 2026-10-01 — no registry release since. Endpoint re-checked 2026-10-01: https://mcp-lab.thefilmradar.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource returns resource metadata naming itself the authorization server, header bearer only. The vendor docs now list 37 tools in six groups (up from 34 in August), including location management — create, delete, restyle, panorama, image analysis — and lab_delete_location is a destructive tool, so scope your agent's permissions accordingly. Tool names come from those docs, not from a tools/list this directory could read, because there is no anonymous access. Closed source, no repo, one operator, and the docs and UI are German-first — the MCP page is entirely in German, which is friction if your agent or your crew is not. It also does not name the models behind lab_generate and lab_animate ('Soul Cinema' is a house label, not an engine), so you are buying credits without knowing which engine renders them; Martini and Nomi both publish their model rosters. Billing is per run with the price quoted first: reads, browsing, previews and project creation are free, while generation, animation, locations and exports draw on credits bought in the Composer. Correction to earlier notes here: the MCP page now states credits are valid for three months (AGB § 7), so do not stockpile them.

name: Cinegenta Studio
tagline: Hosted screenplay-to-production MCP with free planning and quotes, then a greenlit run under a server-enforced cap.
description: Cinegenta's remote MCP works from the script down rather than the shot up: put_script stores the screenplay, build_plan turns it into scenes, cast, wardrobe, props, staging and shots, and quote returns a free itemised estimate. greenlight starts the capped production run, with the cap rechecked before each render; review returns cast and storyboard contact sheets when called, while regenerate is a separate billed image action. The full 13-tool catalog is split across read, write and spend scopes; a restricted key sees only the tools its scopes permit, and a key without spend scope cannot bill.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http cinegenta https://cinegenta.com/api/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer cg_sk_YOUR_KEY"

auth.key_url: https://cinegenta.com/connect — mints a cg_sk_ key with selectable read, write and spend scopes, shown once; the server also accepts it as X-API-Key.

caveats: Beta from a domain registered May 2026 with no public repo or named team, and cap enforcement and refunds remain vendor claims.
Packs run $5 to $500 on the website only; the pricing page no longer states a per-credit price or per-minute range, just a pre-batch estimate.
A key without spend scope cannot bill, so mint scoped keys; the key is shown once.
Stateless POST-only transport with no SSE.
notes: Re-checked 2026-10-27 against cinegenta.com/mcp: endpoint, connect line, Bearer cg_sk_ auth, key minting at cinegenta.com/connect and the 13 tools (4 read, 6 write, 3 billed: greenlight, run_control, regenerate) are unchanged; transport is streamable HTTP with JSON responses, specs 2025-03-26 and 2025-06-18, stateless with no SSE and no sessions. Pricing drifted in presentation: the pricing page now lists only one-time $5, $25, $100 and $500 packs whose credits do not expire, says rates vary by generation options, and shows an estimate per batch instead of the $0.10-per-credit figure and under-a-dollar-to-over-twenty-per-minute range quoted at first listing — so read the quote, not a rate card. Originally verified 2026-09-15: an unauthenticated JSON-RPC POST returns 401 with a proper WWW-Authenticate challenge, GET returns 405, and the server card at cinegenta.com/.well-known/mcp/server-card.json and the official MCP registry entry (com.cinegenta/studio v1.1.0) publish the same endpoint. What we could not check without a scoped key and a spend: whether cap enforcement, failed-render refunds and regenerate's idempotency protection behave as described — those remain vendor claims. Know what you are buying into: the domain was registered in May 2026, the site header still says Beta, and no public repo or named team appears on the site or in the docs. Submission #47 was discovery input, not a verification source.

name: Framesail
tagline: Hosted MCP that carries a script through storyboard, voiceover and shots to a cut MP4.
description: Framesail's own remote MCP exposes its six-stage pipeline to an agent: derive a look from reference images, video or a YouTube link, write or generate the script, lock reference images for every character, place and prop, record voiceover with word-level timing, plan the storyboard scene by scene, then render each shot against those locked references and export with captions, music and SFX. State lives server-side, so a run can pause between chat sessions and resume, and an agent can read or rewrite the script, references and storyboard before the next stage runs. Aimed at long-form output rather than clips, which makes it one of the few studio-class servers an agent can drive end to end.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http framesail https://api.framesail.com/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer fsk_YOUR_KEY"

auth.key_url: https://framesail.com/developers — Claude Code and Cursor use an fsk_ bearer token; claude.ai, Claude Desktop and the mobile app connect over OAuth instead and need no key.

caveats: No free tier, and MCP is not on the entry plan: API and MCP access starts at Pro ($63 a month, billed quarterly).
Credits expire two months after they are granted, so a quiet month is a forfeited month.
Only three tool names are published, and it is hosted only with no way to audit which upstream model the pipeline uses.
Pick one surface per run; the vendor says not to mix MCP and REST.
notes: Re-checked 31 Oct 2026 against the vendor's own pages: the endpoint, HTTP transport, both auth paths (fsk_ bearer key or browser OAuth) and the connect command on framesail.com/developers are unchanged, and the daily probe still gets a 401 from api.framesail.com/mcp, so the server is live and gated. Two things moved since the 18 Sep listing. Prices went up at the bottom of the ladder: quarterly billing now runs Creator $35/month (19,500 credits), Pro $63/month (35,000), Studio $137/month (80,000) and Scale $551/month (330,000), there is still no free tier, and API and MCP access still starts at Pro. And the published tool names changed: the developers page now shows script_generate, storyboard_generate and export_video, where it previously said generate_script and generate_storyboard — so prompts or allowlists written against the old names need updating. Monthly and top-up credits roll over but expire two months after they are granted, so a quiet month is a forfeited month. Only those three tool names are published, so tools_sample lists them rather than a number; third-party directories quote a tool count the vendor does not, and we did not run tools/list without a paid key. Hosted only: no repo, no local package, nothing to self-host, and no way to audit what the pipeline sends to which upstream model. The vendor also ships a REST API over the same stages and says to pick one surface per run rather than mixing MCP and REST. If you want the same script-to-cut arc with a timeline you can actually edit, compare martini; if you only need the breakdown and prompts and will generate elsewhere, penshot does that part for free.

name: Frameo MCP
tagline: Hosted AI production studio: projects, shots, voice, music, lip-sync and the cut behind one OAuth connection.
description: Frameo's official remote server exposes its whole studio: an agent creates a project and modules, generates shots with the video and image models Frameo hosts (Seedance, Kling, Veo), adds voiceover, music, sound effects and lip-sync, keeps saved characters consistent across shots, and handles the cut with frame extraction, ffmpeg trims, subtitles and motion-graphics titles. Every result lands on the project's canvas in the Frameo app, and bundled skills give agents step-by-step production workflows. For a film agent it is one of the few places where generation, continuity and assembly share one project state.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http frameo https://mcp.frameo.ai/mcp

auth.key_url: https://frameo.ai/mcp (sign in with a Frameo account on first call)

caveats: Every paid generation needs an estimate_cost quote first, single-use for 15 minutes; analyze_media is the one paid tool without a quote.
Per-generation costs are not published outside the app, and credits come from a Frameo workspace plan.
The marketing leans toward UGC ads and social video, so expect templates tuned for that; closed source and hosted only.
notes: Checked 10 Oct 2026: the endpoint answers initialize with a proper OAuth 2.1 challenge, the official MCP Registry lists ai.frameo/frameo, and the tool reference at mcp.frameo.ai/docs is generated from the live tool list (58 tools). No tools were run because there is no anonymous path. Every paid generation needs an estimate_cost quote first and the quote is single-use for 15 minutes; analyze_media is the one paid tool without a quote. Pricing is credits from a Frameo workspace plan and per-generation costs are not published outside the app. The company behind it is Dashverse; the marketing leans toward UGC ads and social video, so expect templates tuned for that. Closed source, hosted only.

name: invideo MCP Server
tagline: Official hosted MCP for invideo's cloud editor: agents edit real NLE timelines with branches while you watch.
description: invideo rebuilt its MCP around its browser editor: an agent opens a project by URL, brings media in, edits a real NLE timeline with color, audio and 3D tools, generates with the image, video, voice and music models invideo hosts, and exports, while the user watches each edit land in the editor and can take over by hand. Projects carry a main timeline, branches and a full edit history, so changes can be proposed for review before they reach main. The same surface ships as an Apache-2.0 CLI for shells and coding agents that want files on disk. The old anonymous one-tool script-to-video server is gone: everything now runs in the user's own invideo account and credits.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http invideo https://mcp.invideo.io/mcp
install.cli: curl -fsSL https://agents.invideo.io | sh && invideo auth login

caveats: Needs the user's invideo account: every request but ping answers a sign-in challenge, and work bills that account's credits.
Plans start at Starter, $20 a month for 400 credits per seat; the pricing page lists no free plan, and Seedance 2.5 needs a higher tier.
Tools are not listed without sign-in, so the public sample is the two the vendor guide names; call get_help once connected.
notes: Changed under the listing between September and October 2026. On 23 Sep an unauthenticated POST to https://mcp.invideo.io/mcp completed a handshake and listed one tool, generate-video-from-script. On 27 Oct the same POST returns 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata=…`, the protected-resource document names pro-api-auth.invideo.io as the authorization server, and the error text points agents at a device sign-in flow. mcp.film's daily endpoint check caught the change. The vendor's agent guide (mcp.invideo.io/mcp/agents.md) now describes a cloud video editor ('Figma and GitHub for video'): projects with a main timeline, branches and edit history, opened by URL, with the user watching edits land live. Connect: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, VS Code, claude.ai custom connectors and ChatGPT developer-mode connectors are documented; in Claude Code the sign-in is `/mcp` → invideo → Authenticate after a restart. Agents with no browser use RFC 8628 device sign-in (user approves a code on their own device; tokens last about a day and refresh tokens rotate). The CLI (github.com/invideoio/cli, Apache-2.0, one native binary also on npm and PyPI as `invideo`, 0.1.1 on 27 Oct) covers projects, notebook pages, edits and branches, assets, `gen run` with `--dry-run` pricing and `--max-credits`, stock library search and exports; its README says the CLI and MCP are the same invideo. Pricing (invideo.io/pricing, 27 Oct): Starter $20/seat/month for 400 credits, Plus $60 for 2,000, higher tiers above; Starter has Lite-only agent access and no Seedance 2.0/2.5. Not checked: the signed-in tool list, which needs an account; tools_sample lists only get_help and list_projects, the two the guide names. Re-categorised from Video Generation to Full-Stack AI Studios because the server now holds the project, timeline, generation and review in one place.
